title: Car rental insurance in Poland: what zero excess means
seo_title: Car Rental Insurance in Poland: Zero Excess Explained
meta_description: Understand zero-excess car rental insurance in Poland, common exclusions and what to do after an incident. Practical guidance and personal support from Idan.
content:
Zero excess removes your excess for covered damage. It does not remove the rental conditions, the deposit or your responsibility to report an incident.

I am Idan, a representative of local car rental companies in Poland. My offers include supplier protection with zero excess for covered damage, including theft, glass and wheels, subject to the agreed conditions. I explain those conditions before you book and remain your contact if you need help.

What does SCDW mean?

SCDW stands for Super Collision Damage Waiver. In everyday terms, the rental company waives the excess you would otherwise pay for covered damage. Companies use different package names, so compare the actual protection in your quotation rather than relying on the words “full insurance”.

Protection supplied by the rental company is different from a separate reimbursement policy. With reimbursement cover, you may have to pay the rental company first and then claim the money back from another provider. Check which arrangement an offer includes.

What is not covered by the insurance?

Even with zero excess, the following are not covered by the insurance:

  • Traffic and parking fines, road tolls and related administrative charges.
  • A dirty interior, exceptional cleaning, smoking damage or damage to the interior, subject to the rental agreement's provisions for accident damage.
  • Damage caused deliberately or by intentional misuse of the vehicle.
  • Using the vehicle for a purpose or in a way prohibited by the rental agreement, including driving on unsuitable or restricted tracks.
  • Damage caused while driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
  • Lost keys or vehicle documents, and putting the wrong fuel in the car.
  • Driving by an unauthorised driver or failing to follow the required incident-reporting procedure.

The rental company's agreement sets out the full exclusions and applicable charges. These costs are separate from the protection for covered damage, and liability is not necessarily limited to the deposit.

Two mistakes that are easy to avoid

Wrong fuel: before filling up, check the fuel label and the vehicle information. If you realise you have used the wrong fuel, stop and contact the rental company's assistance service before starting or continuing to drive.

Missing keys: keep the vehicle keys and documents secure. Replacing a key and getting it to you can involve more than the price of the key itself. These examples illustrate exclusions; they are not a price list.

What to do if something happens

  1. Make sure everyone is safe and contact emergency services when necessary.
  2. Follow the rental company's incident instructions promptly, including any requirement for a police report. Do not assume a small scratch needs no report.
  3. Record the location, take photographs when safe and keep relevant documents.
  4. Contact the company's assistance number for operational help. Contact me with your reservation number so I can help coordinate with the company.

My role is to help you understand the next step and work with the supplier on a solution. The company assesses coverage under the rental agreement.

Does this cover a trip outside Poland?

Do not assume that domestic cover automatically includes every country or assistance service abroad. Permission to cross a border, damage protection, towing and a replacement vehicle are separate points to confirm. Read the guide to driving abroad before choosing a company for a multi-country trip.

Why is there still a deposit?

A deposit can secure obligations outside the damage cover, such as fuel or other agreed return conditions. It is separate from the excess. The amount and card requirements should be clear before you book. See how rental deposits work.

Your questions, answered

Does zero excess mean I can never be charged?

No. It applies to covered events under the agreed terms. Excluded damage and other contractual charges can still apply.

Will I need to buy another package at collection?

Your quotation should identify the protection already included. If the collection agent offers something additional and you are unsure, ask what it adds and contact me before agreeing.

Can Idan help after the booking?

Yes. You remain my client after choosing an offer. Keep your reservation number and my contact details alongside the rental company's assistance details.

title: Car rental deposits in Poland: cards, holds and release
seo_title: Car Rental Deposits in Poland: Cards, Holds and Release
meta_description: Why a deposit is required with zero-excess car hire, which card to bring and how release works. Clear guidance for international visitors renting in Poland.
content:
A security deposit is separate from the rental price and insurance excess. Check the amount, accepted card and release process before you arrive in Poland.

I am Idan, your contact with the rental company. When you book through me, the deposit is part of the offer we discuss before you choose a car. The purpose is to make the commitment clear before collection.

Why a deposit if insurance has zero excess?

Zero excess concerns covered vehicle damage. The deposit can secure other obligations in the rental agreement, such as returning the car with the agreed fuel level or meeting the return and cleaning conditions. At some airports, the parking ticket is also part of the return procedure.

The deposit is not the same as an insurance excess. It is also not a universal limit on what a customer could owe for excluded damage or a breach of the agreement. Read the insurance guide for the distinction.

How much will be held?

The amount depends on the rental company, vehicle category and selected package. Your quotation should state the deposit separately from the total rental price. There is no single amount that applies to every offer.

When comparing options, look at both figures: what you pay for the rental and how much available card credit you need for the deposit. If a lower deposit matters to you, mention it in the quotation request.

Which card should you bring?

  • Bring an accepted credit card in the driver's name, as required by the chosen company.
  • Check that enough credit is available for the deposit as well as your other travel spending.
  • Confirm the expiry date, PIN and whether your card can be used for the required transaction abroad.
  • Ask in advance about debit cards, prepaid cards, virtual cards or a card belonging to someone else. Do not assume they will be accepted.

Cash should not be treated as a substitute for the required deposit card. If your card situation is unusual, tell me before booking so I can check it with the company. Paying for the rental and providing its deposit can have different requirements.

A hold and a payment are different

With a pre-authorisation, the deposit reduces your available card credit without necessarily becoming a completed payment. Your bank's app may show it as pending or reserved. The way it appears depends on your card issuer.

Some transactions can instead be processed as an actual charge, depending on the company and card. Ask which method is being used and retain the card-terminal receipt. A charged deposit needs a refund process rather than simply cancelling a hold.

When will the deposit become available again?

There are two stages: the rental company releases the authorisation or processes the refund, and the card issuer updates your account. These do not always happen at the same time.

I do not promise the same number of days for customers from every country. Processing depends on the company, return checks, card issuer and transaction type. Ask for the expected timeframe for your booking and contact your issuer if the hold remains after the company confirms release.

What should you keep?

  • Your reservation and rental agreement.
  • The deposit receipt and vehicle return confirmation.
  • Photographs of the fuel level and the returned car, where practical.
  • Any written confirmation that the company released the deposit.

If you need help, send me your reservation number and the relevant receipt or bank transaction information with sensitive card details hidden. I can follow up with the rental company. Your bank controls when released funds become available on your card.

Your questions, answered

Is the deposit included in the advertised rental total?

It should be shown separately. A refundable deposit is not the same as the rental charge. Your offer should make both clear.

Can I use my travelling companion's card?

Do not assume so. The named-driver and card-holder requirements must be confirmed before collection.

What if I receive a request for bank details for a refund?

Contact me or the rental company through a known contact channel to verify the request before sharing information. Never send your full card details or security code.

title: Driving a rental car from Poland to another country
seo_title: Driving a Rental Car Abroad from Poland: What to Check
meta_description: Planning a cross-border rental from Poland? Check country permission, insurance, towing, replacement cars and road tolls before you book with Idan.
focus_keyword: driving a rental car abroad from Poland
content:
Tell me every country you plan to visit before booking. Permission to drive abroad and the help you receive after a breakdown are different parts of the rental.

Poland is a convenient starting point for a multi-country trip. As your rental-company representative, I can check the route against the available offers and explain the differences that matter beyond the headline price.

Start with your complete route

Include the countries you will visit and those you will only drive through. State where you want to collect and return the car. A return in another country is a separate arrangement from a round trip that starts and ends in Poland.

Do not assume that membership of the EU or Schengen area is enough to permit the journey. The company's authorised destinations and your booking conditions still matter. Obtain the required approval and arrange any applicable payment before crossing the border.

Four things to confirm in writing

  1. Permission: are all your destination and transit countries authorised?
  2. Damage protection: does the agreed zero-excess package apply to the journey?
  3. Towing and recovery: what happens if the car cannot be driven outside Poland, and who pays?
  4. A replacement car: where can you collect it, and is delivery abroad included?

A cross-border fee does not by itself answer all four questions. The quotation and confirmation should identify the selected arrangement, rather than leaving you to discover it during a problem.

Why the assistance package matters: Kaizen Rent

My Hebrew guidance describes a change introduced on 01.04.2026: ordinary permission to travel abroad and the extended VIP ABROAD arrangement provide different assistance. Under the ordinary arrangement described there, getting a replacement car may require reaching a branch in Poland, and recovery outside Poland is not included in the same way. The extended arrangement adds towing and replacement-car assistance abroad under its conditions.

This is why I ask about the journey before recommending an offer. Ask me which arrangement is available for your dates and route, what it costs and what the company confirms in writing. The company's published English fee schedule also lists permission to travel abroad as a specific item. Public website packages and a representative's agreed offer should not be assumed identical.

Collecting or returning outside Poland

Tell me this at the start. International delivery or collection may involve a driver travelling to another country, a separate charge and advance payment. Confirm the amount and payment deadline before accepting the offer.

CarFree also has a Prague branch. A rental collected and returned in Prague is a Czech rental: leaving the Czech Republic then needs to be checked as cross-border travel. Prague to Warsaw, or Warsaw to Prague, is an international route. The rental's base country matters.

Road tolls and vignettes are separate

Rental permission does not pay road tolls. Check the official road operator for every country on your route. For example, Austria's ASFINAG explains its vignette requirement for qualifying vehicles using motorways and expressways.

Toll requirements depend on the road, vehicle category and local system, not simply on having foreign number plates. Check the registration number, country of registration and start date carefully when arranging a digital vignette. Some roads have separate charges.

Documents and collection checklist

  • Check licence requirements for your issuing country and every destination, including whether an International Driving Permit is needed.
  • Keep the rental agreement, written cross-border authorisation and the vehicle documents supplied by the company.
  • Ask the company which original documents or copies are required for your route.
  • Save the rental company's assistance number and my contact details before leaving.
  • If your route changes, contact us before entering an unapproved country.

Your questions, answered

Can I decide to drive abroad after collecting the car?

Ask before crossing. The company must confirm the required authorisation, cover and any charge. Do not assume it can be added retrospectively.

Does Idan's VIP service mean every assistance package is identical?

No. You receive my personal support whichever company you choose, while the supplier's towing, recovery and replacement-car obligations depend on the package you book.

What should I put in the request?

List your countries, collection and return points, dates and times. Mention a one-way journey or any unusual plan so I can check it before preparing the offer.
